arc: the C5 investigation (owner-directed): is m004's Mostow structure object- or observer-data?
headline: the object/observer boundary at the infinity-place is NOT a definitional choice -- it is a MIRROR-PARITY x DIMENSION law

parity_facts_own_verified.CS_mirror_odd: complex volume conjugates under mirror -> CS(M-bar)=-CS(M); CS=1.8e-15=0 (amphichiral)

the_decider: an archimedean datum is OBJECT-canonical IFF mirror-EVEN AND dimensionless (= well-defined on the un-oriented, scale-free object). The OBSERVER supplies the complement: the mirror-ODD completion (the orientation bit, which once chosen fixes the sign of every odd datum -- CS, torsion sign, complex-volume phase) + the DIMENSIONFUL scale
c5_resolution: C5 is settled by a law, not a choice. The Mostow structure IS object-data (its mirror-even/dimensionless part = the entire geometry: Vol, cusp shape, spectra). This does NOT refute G-IDENT/the adelic place-split; the charter's binary ('object-data => G-IDENT fails') is a FALSE DICHOTOMY -- the geometry being object-data is compatible with the frame (orientation+scale) being observer-data, since the frame is exactly the mirror-odd + dimensionful complement. The object reaches the infinity-place with all its even/dimensionless canonical data; the observer supplies only what the object provably cannot self-supply (orientation via amphichirality B1163, scale via the scale-free no-go)
what_made_it_investigable: B1167's cusp-shape separator: a SECOND mirror-even object-canonical archimedean datum (2sqrt3 i, sqrt3-flavored). One datum (Vol) can't reveal a law; two can. The sqrt3 also ties the infinity-place geometry to the disc-144/Q(zeta12) ring-class hinge (B1166) -- finite and archimedean object-data share the same sqrt3
